A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Conformal Prediction for Causal Effects of Continuous Treatments. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison. Relocated material and retained figure content could be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic experiments, semi-synthetic TCGA coverage and interval-width results in Appendix C, and MIMIC-III patient interval estimates.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds TCGA comparator results, conformal baseline comparisons, and a relative runtime result.

M1.justification: The propensity-shift calibration, Gaussian smoothing, optimization objectives, interval construction, and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. Appendix B adds optional numerical-stability advice, without establishing a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same two synthetic datasets, semi-synthetic TCGA data, and MIMIC-III ventilation outcomes. Added comparator experiments retain this coverage; treatment binarization is part of a comparator's preprocessing.

E2.justification: v4 introduces the first evaluated conformal alternatives: vanilla CP in Appendix H and Lei and Candès's binary-treatment CP in Appendix C. It also adds MC dropout and ensembles to the TCGA comparison, which previously reported only the proposed method. This materially broadens the comparator set.

E3.justification: The new Lei and Candès comparison uses binarized treatments, introducing preprocessing for that comparison. The binarization threshold and full comparison settings are unspecified. Existing splits, metrics, intervention values, and training budgets are retained; expanded TCGA generation details do not establish a changed experiment.

E4.justification: The new vanilla-CP control in Appendix H tests the necessity of accounting for intervention-induced distribution shift by omitting that adjustment. Existing interval case studies are retained. The added optimizer-stability discussion does not include new empirical robustness tests.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50 random-seed runs for synthetic experiments and mean/standard-deviation reporting in appendix tables. Added results follow the existing reporting practice. No changed run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained. v4 adds TCGA baseline coverage, vanilla-CP failure findings with mean width 0.0003, and a new comparison reporting widths 0.6255 for the proposed method and 3.2876 for Lei and Candès on binarized treatments. Appendix H also reports MIMIC computation taking roughly ten times longer than MC intervals. These are supplementary results, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix B corrects overall runtime complexity from adding binary-search and solver costs to multiplying them, accounting for repeated solver calls. The principal coverage theorems and proofs are substantively retained; the additional expression for the pinball loss is equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the claims of model-agnostic finite-sample conformal prediction for continuous-treatment potential outcomes with known or estimated propensities, an interval-computation algorithm, and empirical validation.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds practical guidance on single-treatment, univariate-outcome applicability and conservative selection of the propensity-error bound M. Appendix E.2 clarifies population-marginal coverage despite patient-specific intervals. Appendix B adds numerical failure conditions involving low overlap, underflow, and unstable optimization.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies Gaussian treatment and outcome means for the existing TCGA experiment. Appendix B adds log-domain stabilization guidance, and Appendix H adds relative MIMIC runtime information. Existing hardware, model architecture, training settings, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Tan's 2006 propensity-score paper is removed from the bibliography, leaving an unresolved citation in the discussion of M. Appendix C adds empirical positioning against Lei and Candès based on interval width. Most other reference changes are formatting or publication-metadata updates for retained works.

P1.justification: v4 adds a NeurIPS checklist and several explanatory passages, and separates the former background appendix into background and extended discussion, shifting subsequent appendix letters. Author, bibliography, and equation-reference formatting also change. The main narrative remains largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a Method column and grouped comparator rows. Some captions, tables, and figures are repositioned, and the author block is reformatted. All twelve figure graphics are retained; the changes primarily concern table expansion and page reflow.

improvement.justification: v4 improves empirical context through relevant conformal controls and TCGA baselines, clarifies practical coverage conditions, supplies additional generation and numerical guidance, and corrects runtime complexity. The gains are limited by incomplete settings for the new binary-treatment comparison and an introduced unresolved citation. The core method and existing empirical findings remain unchanged.
